## Verdict: REJECT (one Important checklist FAIL: the changelog says memory is never written under a rule-set file, but retrieval usage counters still are)
The PR is not ready to merge: `changelog.d/389.added.md` says SQL Lens saves nothing to memory while a rule-set file is configured, but `build_agent` builds `ChromaAgentMemory` with `track_usage=allow_memory_writes` before the rule-set override, so retrieval still writes hit counts and timestamps.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major
- VC-1: FAIL (important) — The changelog says that while a rule-set file is configured SQL Lens saves nothing to memory; no memory write (save tools, retrieval usage counters or timestamps) happens under a rule-set file. [changelog.d/389.added.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  In src/sqllens/agent/factory.py build_agent, ChromaAgentMemory is built at line 149-153 with track_usage=allow_memory_writes (line 152), which is still the caller's value (default True). The rule-set override `allow_memory_writes = allow_memory_writes and rule_sets is None` only comes at line 189, after the memory object is constructed, and it only gates the two save-tool registrations (190, 206). With a rule-set file configured and the default call build_agent(cfg), track_usage is therefore True. In agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py:313-327 each retrieval then bumps hit_count and last_hit_date and calls collection.update. That is a memory write under a rule-set file, so changelog.d/389.added.md:8-9 ('While a rule-set file is configured, SQL Lens saves nothing to memory') is not true for retrieval usage counters and timestamps. The docstring at factory.py:90-97 describes the same gap: counters are disabled only when allow_memory_writes=False is passed explicitly.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
